entries.title: Bring a friend
items: Play together: press Play together on the title screen, or Bring a friend on the menu, and your town opens up for friends. They join with a four-letter code, a link or a QR code. Up to eight people in one town.
A friend can bring a person they made, make one on the spot, or take anyone free in your town. That person stays in town when they go.
Parties work across players. Invite a friend or ask to join theirs, follow the leader on foot, share a car, and if you fall behind you catch up.
The party leader can take back anyone at any moment, even a car at full speed. It carries on down the road without a jump.
Split off to start your own party whenever you like, keep who you are playing, and rejoin later.
The host decides what each friend may do: take people, spend money, drive cars, change settings, Direct and Stir. Five plain switches, one player at a time.
One clock for everyone. Going faster or skipping the night needs everybody to agree.
If your connection drops you keep your person, and you are back as soon as it returns. When everyone leaves, the town goes to sleep and wakes with the same code.
It is still your town: take it home whenever you like and carry on alone, exactly where it was. Nobody has to sign in to any of this.

entries.title: Make yourself
items: Make your own person: race, body, face, hair, clothes, nature, quirk, voice and a name, or press Random. Move them into a home of their own, or in with a family from the gallery.
You can also change anyone who already lives here: pick them, press Tell them, then Change how they look.
People get changed now. Work clothes for work, nightwear for bed, something smart for dinner, sportswear for the gym, and a coat on a cold day.
New clothes for every job in town, and a whole new wardrobe: everyday, smart, sport, swim, winter, party and night.
The gallery has 24 households now, and every face in it is a real picture of that person.
Tall folk duck as they go through a door instead of shrinking in a blink.
When someone is playing, Change clothes is on the list. Find a door first: nobody changes on the pavement.

entries.title: People are funny
items: Over a thousand new things to say, about the fire last week, the job, the date, the hedge. Nobody says the same line twice inside five days.
People make friends, fall in love, marry and move in together, whether you are watching or not.
Feuds start for a reason and get worse: words, pranks, a sign in the yard, a row in the street, a hearing at the town hall. They can also end, sometimes with a rescue or a wedding.
Dates, proposals, rows and weddings really happen somewhere. When one starts near you or to your family, press Watch for a little staged scene with voices.
Quirks now change what people do. A person afraid of ducks stays out of the park, and a shower singer annoys the household.
Each of the nine races has a want of its own. Elves wilt without something green. Orcs enjoy a good row.
Four small spells: Tidy, Warm, Mend and Hush. They work better in a good mood. In a bad one, keep an eye on the curtains.
New on the Phone: Who's Who shows how everyone stands with each other. The Story now tells a family's goings-on as one tale, and the Odd Sheet follows stories from issue to issue.
More weather over heads: hearts, a red bolt for a feud, Zs when worn out, snow when lonely. From high up, each block of town has its own sign.
Fires are rarer, about one every two or three days.

entries.title: Fixes from a real iPhone
items: On foot, buildings are their real height, with proper pitched roofs. Only a building standing between you and the camera dips out of the way.
Parked cars stay parked. They used to back slowly away, and that is also why a car you called never seemed to be there.
A called car now pulls up close by, and the distance on screen follows the car itself.
Garage doors are taller, so the Trail Jeep fits. Anything too big stands on the drive.
The lights on a moving fire engine stay on the engine.
Sound comes back after you switch tabs, and tapping the screen brings it back if it does not.
The engine hum that played all the time is gone. You only hear an engine when someone is driving.
Tapping a person zooms in so you can really see them.
Flames are tongues of fire now, and they look far better up close.
Buttons no longer cover the job instructions on a phone.

entries.title: Fire
items: Buildings can catch fire now: a stove left on, old wiring, an accident at work, a small spell gone wrong. Fire spreads room to room, smoke fills the place, and it happens whether or not you are looking.
Smoke alarms call the fire station, and an engine comes down the real road with its siren on. Other cars pull over. Some alarms have a flat battery, so somebody has to notice.

Be the firefighter. Take someone on shift, run to the engine and drive it, take the hose, connect to a hydrant or use the tank, hold the button and steer the water. Break down jammed doors. Lift people and carry them out.
Leave it alone and the crew does exactly the same work. Take over a firefighter in the middle of a fire and carry on from there.
Burned rooms stay burned until they are mended. Insurance pays, the repairs use boards from the yard, and a family with no home left is moved somewhere until theirs is ready.
Anyone hurt goes to the clinic by ambulance. Nobody dies. People you carry out will remember it.
Moments: when something big happens a card pops up. Press Jump in and you are there, or ignore it and the town deals with it. Nothing ever pauses. Happening now shows them too.
The Odd Sheet, the town paper, comes out every three days with what really happened, and a gossip column. Read it in the Paper app on your Phone.
The Story app on your Phone keeps your household's story so far. Birthdays, dates, rows over the hedge, a very small horse.
Some shops and offices now have extinguishers you can use, and big buildings have sprinklers.

entries.title: First wage
items: There is a timber yard now. Take Timber Lane out of the north-east corner of Oddhaven to Wend Wood and Wend Mill.

Take over a logger and do the job: walk up to a marked tree, swing with the needle in the middle until it comes down, carry the logs on your shoulder to the landing, and pull the lever to send the cart to the mill.
Take over a sawmill hand: carry a log to the bench, pull the lever as it lines up with the blade, stack the boards on the rack. A timber driver takes them to the lumber yard in the truck.
Nobody playing? The crew does the same work on the same trees. Take someone over in the middle of a cut and the half-cut tree is still half cut, and hand back and they carry on.
Doing the work yourself pays about a quarter more. Boards go to the lumber yards, and homes use them for repairs on bills day.
The Phone: bank, jobs, mail, map, calendar and what is going on right now. Bills, wages, promotions and tow gnome invoices all come as real letters. You can take a new job from it too.
Happening now shows the busiest things in town. Tap one to go and look.
Stir things up: drag one person onto another to introduce them, set up a date, start a row or patch it up.
New work clothes: hi-vis vests, hard hats, coveralls, scrubs, chef jackets, aprons and uniforms.

entries.title: Doors open
items: Every building in both towns now opens. Walk in through the door you can see, or tap a house in town view and the roof lifts off.
Real homes: bedrooms, a bathroom, a kitchen, a sofa, and people who use them. They sleep in their own bed, cook at the stove, sit down to eat and queue for the shower.
Shops, cafes, the pub, the gym, offices, the school and the rest all have rooms, with staff at their tills and desks.
New town look: houses with yards and garages, shop fronts with shutters, offices in glass, flats with balconies. Parked cars stand outside homes and shops.
Flats have a lift. Press the button, pick a floor.
Press things: light switches, garage doors, shop shutters. The Rift Lodge has a test room with two levers and a plate. There is something in the strongroom.
Turn the camera with right-drag or Q and E, two fingers on a phone, or the right stick.
Take a passenger and you stay in your seat. Press Get out and the driver pulls over.

entries.title: Jump in
items: Take over anyone in town: tap them, press Take over. It is free, as often as you like, whether they are asleep, at work, out shopping, walking or driving.
Walk with the stick, the keyboard or a controller, or tap the ground and they will walk there along the pavement. Up is always the top of the screen.
Take someone at the wheel and the car is yours, right where it was. Other drivers now brake for you, and for you on foot in the road.
Hand back and they carry on by themselves from wherever you left them. A little card tells you what they just did.
Bring your household or friends along as a party. They follow you, pile into your car while there are seats, and catch up if you leave them behind. Swap who you are playing at any time.
Call one of your household's cars and it turns up at a nearby kerb. Leave it out and the tow gnome takes it home, for a small fee.

entries.title: The street lives
items: Pick a household from the gallery: thirteen of them, all nine peoples, each with a small story of their own.
Three hundred people now live here. They sleep, eat, go to work, pay bills, drive, walk the pavements, sit on their steps and stop for a chat.
The town view: drag to move, pinch to zoom, and run time at 1x, 2x or 4x, or pause it. A little weather sign over each head shows how someone feels.
Tap anyone to see their name, mood, needs and what they are up to. Then tap a place or a person and pick what they should do next, up to three things in a row.
Conversations you can read, and short mutters you can hear. Your own household speaks in full.
Cars now carry real people to real places. Block a road and the tow gnome sorts it out, and sends the bill.
Your town saves itself. Press Continue to carry on, and sign in if you want it on your other devices too. It keeps going while you are away.

entries.title: First drive
items: A small county to drive around: the towns of Oddhaven and Brackenford, with a road and a bridge between them.
Traffic on the roads and people on the pavements. They are stand-ins for now: the town starts living in the next update.
Steer with the stick on a phone, WASD on a keyboard, or a controller.
A top-down view, where up on the stick is always north.
